pr_title: 2nd call to MemoryCache.Set() with the same key same size erases entry if cache is full
pr_comments: @dotnet/area-extensions-caching @mgravell or @sebastienros -- can one you have a look?

issue_context.title: 2nd call to MemoryCache.Set() with the same key erases entry if cache is full
comments: Agreed it appears to be same root case.  Set actually ends up calling CreateEntry.  If you wanted to update an entry you could try calling TryGetValue although here that wouldn't help since your value is not mutable (int).  I suspect that there is something that could be tweaked here to improve the case where two entries are created with the same key name.  We can take a look.

In our case it was simple to adjust the capacity of the cache with `desiredSize + 1` since we know ahead of time how many entries we want to store.
It'd be good to fix it, but I think leaving this as a known bug along with a note in the docs would be pretty acceptable too.

@danmoseley that test covers the case when the size limit is exceeded. In this issue the cache is full but it should be able to replace one entry with another of the same size. This seems like a bug with how the limits are enforced.

I think the issue is that the prior entry is marked as expired, but its size isn't subtracted until after the capacity check:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/22ba36d5b0e78c984d8e0b24ae389cabd345ec30/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory/src/MemoryCache.cs#L129-L132
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/22ba36d5b0e78c984d8e0b24ae389cabd345ec30/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory/src/MemoryCache.cs#L142
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/22ba36d5b0e78c984d8e0b24ae389cabd345ec30/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory/src/MemoryCache.cs#L160

review_comments: Would it be possible to avoid a separate case here by passing priorEntry to `UpdateCacheSizeExceedsCapacity`?  @Tratcher [mentioned in the issue](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/36039#issuecomment-1209969507) that he thought the cause here was that that method didn't consider the size of the evicted item.
I agree, for this case we should run the same logic we run for not exceeding capacity.
